original_value: Understanding a person’s feelings is a very important process for the affective computing. People express their emotions in various ways. Among them, facial expression is the most effective way to present human emotional status. We propose efficient deep joint spatiotemporal features for facial expression recognition based on the deep appearance and geometric neural networks. We apply three-dimensional (3D) convolution to extract spatial and temporal features at the same time. For the geometric network, 23 dominant facial landmarks are selected to express the movement of facial muscle through the analysis of energy distribution of whole facial landmarks.We combine these features by the designed joint fusion classifier to complement each other. From the experimental results, we verify the recognition accuracy of 99.21%, 87.88%, and 91.83% for CK+, MMI, and FERA datasets, respectively. Through the comparative analysis, we show that the proposed scheme is able to improve the recognition accuracy by 4% at least.

result.paraphrase: Recognizing a person’s feelings is an important task in affective computing. Since people convey emotions in many ways, facial expression is the most effective means of showing human emotional state. We present efficient deep joint spatiotemporal features for facial expression recognition using deep appearance and geometric neural networks. A three-dimensional (3D) convolution is used to extract spatial and temporal features simultaneously. In the geometric network, 23 key facial landmarks are chosen to represent facial muscle movement by analyzing the energy distribution across all facial landmarks. These features are merged with a designed joint fusion classifier so they can complement one another. Experimental results confirm recognition accuracies of 99.21%, 87.88%, and 91.83% on the CK+, MMI, and FERA datasets, respectively. Comparative analysis shows that the proposed method improves recognition accuracy by at least 4%.
